replies.author: @Duneenzo
replies.text: Without a couple of fundamental speech instructions your written corrections mean nothing.  If the speaker doesn't know that the Maori A  is always long they can still look at your explanation and say Tacker-hay.  And without stress indicators they can still put the stress on the wrong syllable.  For instance the word 'fundamental' appears in the dictionary as funda'mental.  The little apostrophe indicates that the stressed syllable comes after the mark - fundaMENtal.  Other examples would be for'get, with the get part being stressed.  Without proper language mark-ups it's all still open to personal interpretation.

They can have a Harvard University education paid for by the Casino business.  They're the wealthiest tribe in the Appalachia area of the US.  It's all explained in Peter Santenello's video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ibDrnMg3mbA    It might be that Canadians also have a 'land for rent and income' system with a wealthy business, I just don't know.

Was in Canada in the 1980’s. Lived in Quebec. I was shocked to learn native tribes were living on reservations. 
I was sadly surprised as l thought that level of racism only happened in the USA.
I had always seen Canada more like us with human rights a big priority. Sadly not true.
We have two offical languages Maori and NZ sign language, although English is most commonly used.
From daycare centres, primary, intermediate and high schools, Maori is spoken along with English.
At university one can choose to do a full doctorate in Maori.
I live in a region where all our schools are Te Reo Maori. Approx 65% of our local population are Maori, and it is wonderful to hear Maori spoken from toddlers through to grandparents. My belief is Canada has a very long way to go.
